title: Coordination Note: Strip Allowance for Customers Who Also Hold a CGM Program
content:
Holding a CGM program — a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program — changes the strip allowance of the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program.

While the customer holds a CGM program in active status, strips are supplied for backup and confirmation testing, and the strip allowance is the lower of the treatment-class allowance and the tier's with-CGM allowance. A CGM program in referral received, pending authorization, on hold or closed does not reduce the allowance. The status is read from the customer's CGM program record.

The reduction applies to strips and lancets only, not to control solution, lancing devices or meters, and an over-limit justification record that documents a testing frequency above the reduced allowance lifts it under the payer allowance policy.

| CGM program status | Strip allowance |
|---|---|
| active | the lower of the treatment-class allowance and the with-CGM allowance |
| referral received, pending authorization, on hold, closed, or no CGM program | the treatment-class allowance |

**Example (hypothetical figures).** Treatment-class allowance 450 strips, with-CGM allowance 150 strips: while the CGM program is active the allowance is 150 strips; once that CGM program is on hold it returns to 450. With a treatment-class allowance of 100 strips and a with-CGM allowance of 300 strips, the active CGM program leaves the allowance at 100, the lower of the two.
